captions.instagram:
How does a firefly glow?

A firefly is a beetle with a lamp in its tail that wastes almost nothing as heat. Watch one enzyme turn luciferin, ATP and oxygen into a single yellow-green photon, flip the oxygen switch with a puff of nitric oxide, and make a whole tree of fireflies fall into step.

→ A firefly is a beetle, with a lamp built into the underside of its tail.
→ Luciferin, ATP and oxygen meet inside the enzyme luciferase.
→ Make the mix acidic and the same reaction glows orange-red.
→ A nerve signal makes a puff of nitric oxide, and oxygen floods in: flash.
→ A Photuris female fakes the answer, and eats the male who believes her.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/fireflyclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does a firefly glow? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
A firefly is a beetle with a lamp in its tail that wastes almost nothing as heat. Watch one enzyme turn luciferin, ATP and oxygen into a single yellow-green photon, flip the oxygen switch with a puff of nitric oxide, and make a whole tree of fireflies fall into step.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/fireflyclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/fireflyclear

In this video:
• A beetle with a lamp. A firefly is a beetle.
• Light from chemistry, not heat. Inside each light cell the enzyme luciferase uses ATP to prime luciferin, then oxygen.
• An oxygen switch. The lantern is dark because mitochondria near the air tubes use up the oxygen.
• Codes, liars and synchrony. Each species has a flash code: a common eastern firefly male flashes a J every 6 seconds and his female answers 2 seconds later.
• Fireflies of India and the world. India has at least 92 species, about 60% found nowhere else, most in the Western Ghats.
• How we found out. Boyle saw glowing wood go dark in his air pump in 1667.
